card.name: Verb after a named adverse condition
card.fires_on: The word right after a named adverse reaction or condition as subject (e.g. 'fractures most', 'CDAD has'), where the next word is likely 'commonly', 'been reported' or 'occur'. Mostly in warnings sections.

modes.label: most + adverb
modes.description: The word 'most' after a reaction name, leading into 'commonly' or 'frequently'.
modes.example: Atypical femoral fractures<< most>> commonly occur with minimal or no trauma to

modes.label: has/have after reaction
modes.description: The auxiliary 'has' or 'have' after a reaction or disease name, leading into 'been reported' or 'included'.
modes.example: CDAD<< has>> been reported to occur more than 2

card.writes: It promotes frequency adverbs like 'commonly', 'usually' and 'typically', so it sets up statements about how often or in what way a reaction occurs.
card.plain: It fires after the name of a side effect, when the text is about to say how commonly or in what way it occurs.
